messages.author: 4bcb9c081e2c48eb
messages.subject: How to deal with the variance if it is a matrix in pmf model?
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to implement the pmf model. According to the paper, there is a prior normal distribution over the latent factor of users and items like :

u ~ normal(0,(1/alpha_u) * I)

the alpha_u is a single value and the I is a unit matrix. So the product of them is matrix too. But stan just accept single value or vector. So how can I transform the variance to fit stan's requirement? I also wonder why a unit matrix is multiplied but not a 1*k vector. Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to deal with the variance if it is a matrix in pmf model?
parts:
If u is an N-vector and alpha_u is scalar, you can do this:

u ~ normal(0, 1 / alpha_u);

which is just a more efficient way of writing

for (n in 1:N)
u[n] ~ normal(0, 1 / alpha_u);

Although you can do this:

u ~ multi_normal(0, diag_matrix(rep_vector(N, 1/alpha_u)));

but it works out to the same density but is not nearly
as efficient or easy to read.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to deal with the variance if it is a matrix in pmf model?
parts:
rep_vector produces a vector. I don't know what drag_matrix() does.
Did you mean diag_matrix()? Also, the first argument to multi_normal
must be a vector. The signatures are in the index to the manual and
reproduced in the parser error messages.

What you were trying to do was

u ~ multi_normal(rep_vector(0, N), diag_matrix(rep_vector(1 / alpha_u, N)));

which is much much much more efficiently coded in Stan as

u ~ normal(0, inv(alpha_u));

Or you can use 1 / alpha_u instead of inv(alpha_u), but it's a bit
less efficient.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to deal with the variance if it is a matrix in pmf model?
parts:
Stan is really not ideal for factor models at scale.
It's possible, but it won't scale well with number of dimensions
and data points and it's very hard to get it to converge (and
indexes won't be identified in different chains). The efficient
algorithms to do what you're trying to do tend to work one
rank (singular vectors/value) at a time, fit that, then work
on the residuals. I don't know if it'd be possible to build some
kind of direct model in Stan that would be much more efficient.

At K=30, I think you're going to have problems with speed and
convergence.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to deal with the variance if it is a matrix in pmf model?
parts:
To scale, everyone working on the Netflix prize data singular
value decomposition was using this algorithm:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_Hebbian_Algorithm

with the algorithm description here:

http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.102.2084&rep=rep1&type=pdf

I even implemented it for LingPipe. But it's not really
possible to code this in Stan. You can write the model down in
Stan easily enough, but it's very hard to sample.

If you have small K and a good amount of well-separated data,
then Stan can fit it.

- Bob
